HIST 210
3 March 2026
                         Lincoln's Second Inaugural
Lincoln's Second Inaugural is short, and that is part of its power. He refuses to gloat; he refuses even to blame. Both sides read the same Bible and pray to the same God (Lincoln 2). The address turns from politics to providence, and the turn is the point.
In the final paragraph Lincoln asks for "malice toward none" and "charity for all." These phrases have become so familiar that we forget how strange they sounded in March 1865, with the war nearly won.
                                   Works Cited:
Lincoln, Abraham. "Second Inaugural Address." 4 Mar. 1865. Avalon Project, Yale Law School, avalon.law.yale.edu/19th_century/lincoln2.asp.
White, Ronald C. Lincoln's Greatest Speech: The Second Inaugural. Simon & Schuster, 2002.
